notes: Volume J–L of the collection: 52 pages, 40 entries (9 under J, 12 under K, 19 under L) covering architects, builders, developers, landscape architects, a firm manager and several firms, read end to end — the title page, the three letter indexes, every entry (education, firms, cultural identification, narrative and footnotes), every 'Projects in San Francisco' / 'Works in San Francisco' / 'Projects Overseen in San Francisco' and 'Other notable projects' list, and every figure caption. The fourth of the eight letter-range PDFs; A–C, D–F and G–I are done. No inventory table and no APN anywhere, so the record-parcel check resolve_eas.py's report prints has nothing to test against. Seven entries yielded no numbered San Francisco address: Alfred Henry Jacobs is listed in the J index but the volume carries no biography for him at all; A. Quincy Jones and William Howard Knowles are cross-references to their firms; Frederick and Lois Langhorst and Langhorst & Langhorst have no known San Francisco structures, which the volume says outright; Ernest Kump's two San Francisco projects are given by shipyard and by cross street; Donnell Jaekle's single entry is the Rivera Street tract already recorded from volume G–I's Henry Horn entry; and Daniel Libeskind's Contemporary Jewish Museum is given without a street number.

coverage.remaining: Volumes M–O, P–R, S–U and V–Z of the same collection — four more PDFs from the same landing page, each its own batch. Volumes A–C, D–F, G–I and J–L are finished.
coverage.note: 148 numbered-address mentions across 52 pages became 125 findings. The gap is the unnumbered and the repeated: eleven project-list lines give a tract, a cross street or a block with no street number ("6 duplexes on Duncan Street", "Herbert Hoover Junior High School, 14th Avenue at Santiago Street", "Earthquake and Fire Cottages"), and the rest are addresses printed twice — the narrative repeating the list, a figure caption naming an address from the entry's own list, and one building, the Miramar Apartments, listed both as 1580-1598 Market Street and as 20 Franklin Street. 105 of the 125 reached a parcel and 20 did not: 11 recorded ranges now split across separate parcels, 5 numbers the city no longer has (927 Market, 585 California, 2353 Mission, 2671 Mission, 2963 Webster — the Vedanta Temple among them) and 4 condominiums. Of the 105, 91 were published onto 90 pages (55 created by this run) across 22 neighborhood directories, and 14 were declined: 12 already carried by a survey or statement that documented the building first, 2 second street numbers on parcels already carrying the fact.
